methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Norfolk native brings free AI workshops to Hampton Roads to close the technology gap - WTKR
signals.signal_reading: Free AI workshops led by a local Norfolk native represent grassroots peer-to-peer knowledge transfer in Hampton Roads, signaling distributed capability-building outside traditional tech hubs through community-driven education rather than platform dependence.

signals.title: Roanoke College launches WorkAI Lab to prepare leaders for new era of technology - Roanoke College
signals.signal_reading: Roanoke College's WorkAI Lab represents institutional investment in deep AI fluency outside NoVA/Richmond metros, potentially seeding distributed capability through workforce training that could activate peer networks in underserved regions.

signals.title: Tech Briefs: Virginia Tech adds an artificial intelligence minor to its curriculum - Cardinal News
signals.signal_reading: Virginia Tech adding an AI minor concentrates deep technical capability in an existing research hub, reinforcing the 'pockets' pattern where educational infrastructure advantages compound rather than distributing AI fluency to adjacent rural communities.

signals.title: ‘Shaping our future’: Company powering AI data centers invests $50+ million in Henrico, adding 200 jobs - WWBT
signals.signal_reading: A $50M+ data center infrastructure investment in Henrico adds 200 jobs but signals shallow AI engagement—physical infrastructure without corresponding workforce capability development, widening the gap between capital investment and distributed AI literacy.

signals.title: TAYLOR: AI data centers increase Virginia’s urban-rural divide - The Cavalier Daily
signals.signal_reading: Student commentary explicitly naming data centers as drivers of urban-rural divide reflects growing awareness that infrastructure concentration in NoVA/metros creates geographic capability gaps without intentional distribution mechanisms or deep local adoption.
